reviewer: Codex computational expert review authorized by the user
decision_basis: Integrated review of paired Rosetta energy origin, direct complex and cross-interface signals, contact and epitope preservation, AntiFold compatibility, NetSolP, NanoMelt, TNP, chemical and structural risk, component controls, and mutation diversity; predictions are ranking evidence rather than experimental validation.

decisions.review_rationale: Retain as the lower-risk R45 component control for selected combinations; standalone binding signal is separated-state-driven, so it is not treated as an affinity-positive result by itself.
Retain as the required component control for several directly supported R45V combinations; standalone high hydrophobic and contact-change risk remains explicit.

Exclude because the mutant complex is unfavorable in all three paired repeats and the apparent binding gain is entirely separated-state-driven, while exposed Trp, oxidation, contact-change, repulsion, and preparation-sensitivity risks are high.

Exclude because the mutant complex is unfavorable in all three paired repeats and the apparent binding gain is entirely separated-state-driven, with added Trp oxidation, contact-change, repulsion, preparation-sensitivity, and negative AntiFold evidence.

Select as a strong affinity hypothesis with favorable complex, separated-state, binding, and cross-interface signals in all repeats; high local hydrophobic and contact-change risk requires experimental testing.
Select as the complementary E105 affinity hypothesis with favorable complex, separated-state, binding, and cross-interface signals; retain explicit hydrophobic and local packing risk.

Select as a component control and distinct affinity hypothesis because complex and direct binding signals are favorable, while separated-state, hydrophobization, contact-change, and negative AntiFold cautions remain.

Select as a unique position-114 affinity hypothesis with favorable complex and direct binding signals; high hydrophobic, oxidation, contact-change, and repulsion risks prevent interpreting it as validated improvement.
Select because complex, separated-state, binding, and cross-interface energies are all favorable and the combination supplies a property-supported A23S control for the higher-risk E105F hypothesis.
Select because both complex and separated-state scores improve with favorable binding and cross-interface signals, providing a complementary A23S plus E105L combination.
Select as a balanced property-affinity hypothesis: the complex and cross-interface signals improve, AntiFold is favorable, contacts are unchanged, and both component singles are retained.

Select as a deliberately property-led combination with three material property improvements, favorable AntiFold, unchanged contacts, and retained component controls; its binding gain is separated-state-driven and remains low confidence.
Select as a property-led and mechanistically distinct combination with two property improvements, favorable AntiFold, unchanged contacts, and both single controls; direct complex support is absent.
Select because the complex and cross-interface signals improve and Q1D provides a low-risk property component; separated-state contribution and negative AntiFold evidence remain cautions.
Select as a property-affinity combination with favorable binding, cross-interface, and AntiFold signals plus retained component controls; inconsistent complex improvement limits confidence.

Select only as a lower-confidence property-combination hypothesis that preserves non-E105 mechanistic diversity and has retained single controls; complex energy is strongly unfavorable and binding evidence is weak.

Exclude because the mutant complex is strongly unfavorable and the apparent binding gain is entirely separated-state-driven while carrying the high-risk R45V substitution; A23S;R45V supplies a better directly supported alternative.

Select as a distinct two-affinity-component hypothesis with strong binding and cross-interface signals, unchanged contacts, and both single controls; near-neutral complex energy and negative AntiFold evidence require caution.
Select as a property-led combination with favorable AntiFold, unchanged contacts, and retained controls; complex energy is unfavorable and the apparent binding gain is separated-state-driven.
Select as one of the strongest direct complex and cross-interface combinations with unchanged contacts; both hydrophobic component risks and negative AntiFold evidence remain explicit.
Select as the complementary E105L combination with strong complex, binding, cross-interface, and AntiFold support and unchanged contacts, while retaining component hydrophobicity cautions.
Select because the complex and direct binding signals improve and two property indicators are favorable; contact review, negative AntiFold, and combined hydrophobization risks remain.
Select as a property-compatible E105L combination with strongly favorable AntiFold and unchanged contacts; complex energy does not improve and the binding signal is separated-state-driven.
Select as a non-E105 property-combination hypothesis with retained controls and unchanged contacts; complex, AntiFold, and weak cross-interface evidence make it lower priority.
Retain as a low-risk property single and component control for selected combinations; its standalone apparent binding gain is separated-state-driven and not direct affinity support.
Select as a property single and component control with favorable complex and separated-state scores; binding is neutral and proximity to the experimental coordinate gap remains a structural caution.

Select as a property single with two material improvements and favorable AntiFold plus value as a combination control; standalone complex energy is unfavorable and the site is adjacent to the coordinate gap.

Select as a distinct property single with two material improvements and favorable AntiFold; standalone complex and cross-interface evidence are unfavorable and the site is adjacent to the coordinate gap.
Select as a property single and component control for selected F30T combinations; direct affinity evidence is neutral to unfavorable and the site is adjacent to the coordinate gap.
Select as a property single and component control with favorable AntiFold; binding and complex energies are not favorable and the CDR glycine flexibility change requires experimental evaluation.

Promote from reserve because complex and direct binding signals improve, two property indicators are favorable, contacts are unchanged, and it replaces the weaker Q1D;R45V hypothesis without increasing R45V representation.
Keep as a reserve because complex and AntiFold signals are favorable, but no property change reaches the material threshold and E105L is already represented at the predefined diversity cap.
Promote from reserve because complex, binding, and cross-interface energies are directly favorable with unchanged contacts and retained single controls, while adding an underrepresented F30T pairing.

Promote from reserve as a strong direct affinity combination with favorable complex and cross-interface energies, unchanged contacts, no material property adverse signal, and retained component controls.
Keep as a reserve despite strong complex and binding evidence because one material property signal is adverse and adding it would exceed the predefined E105L component-diversity cap.

Keep as a reserve because complex and cross-interface energies improve, but one material property signal is adverse and E105F is already represented at the predefined diversity cap by stronger complementary combinations.
